title: Ananaspudding (1st Recipe) (Pineapple Pudding)
description: A pudding made with pineapple, egg whites, and milk.
steps: Mix the maizena with some cold milk into a thin paste, without lumps.
Bring the remaining milk to a boil, add the sugar and, stirring vigorously, the mixed maizena and let the pudding cook through while stirring for 3 to 4 minutes.
Then mix it away from the fire with the stiffly beaten egg white.
Make sure that in the meantime the pineapple is pitted and cut into small pieces, stir the pineapple through the pudding, but keep some pieces aside to mix through the sauce.
Pour the mixture into a mold rinsed with cold water and let it become cold and firm.
Bring the pineapple liquid to a boil, add sugar to taste and bind it with some mixed sago.
After cooling, stir the remaining pineapple pieces through it and serve the sauce with the pudding.
Color the sauce rose if desired by dissolving 1/2 sheet red gelatine in it.

title: Ananaspudding (2nd Recipe) (Pineapple Pudding)
description: A pudding made with pineapple, whipped cream, and egg whites.

ingredients.name: 1/2 tin pineapple with 1 1/2 to 2 dl liquid
12 g white gelatine or 10 g powdered gelatine

steps: Cut the pineapple into pieces and remove pits if necessary.
Dissolve the gelatine (which has soaked 10 to 15 minutes in cold water) in the pineapple liquid.
Let this mixture cool somewhat and add it to the cream, which has been beaten stiff with the sugar.
Mix this with the stiffly beaten egg whites.
Stir the pineapple pieces and the scraped vanilla through it at the same time and let the mass stand, stirring from time to time, until it becomes jelly-like and the pineapple pieces no longer sink.
Then pour it into a mold brushed with unbeaten egg white and let the pudding become cold and firm.
Turn it out onto a damp plate.
Garnish the pudding with jelly made from pineapple liquid (see fruit jelly recipe 566) and with pineapple pieces.

description: A bread preparation made with bread, anchovies, and butter or margarine.

description: Prepared with artichokes and lemon.
steps: Remove the stem from the artichokes, take out the ugly leaves and cut off the withered tips from the remaining ones.
Wash them, halve the large ones and bind them crosswise with twine.

Let the balls rise, covered with a somewhat damp cloth, for another 20 minutes to ½ hour.

title: Caramelsaus (Caramel Sauce)
description: A sauce made with cream, milk, and sugar.
steps: Bring the milk with the cream to a boil.
Put 125 g sugar in a fairly large pan and let it stand on a not too fierce fire until it has become caramel and begins to foam over the entire surface.
Then slowly pour, all in one stream, the boiling liquid into it, off the fire.
Add 25 g sugar.
Beat the eggs, add them slowly, stirring constantly and rubbing away lumps, to the maizena.
Add to this mixture carefully, stirring constantly, enough of the hot liquid until the eggs are thoroughly warmed.
Pour it back into the pan and let the sauce, stirring vigorously with a whisk, boil for 3-4 minutes on a gentle fire.

Stir the egg yolks with the cornstarch and 25 grams sugar, if necessary also a few spoonfuls of milk into a smooth paste.
Pour the paste into the caramel milk and let the custard cook through while stirring with a whisk (3 to 4 minutes).

Beat the egg yolks with 25 g sugar, carefully add, while stirring constantly, enough of the hot liquid so that the egg yolks are well warmed.

title: Duitse zandtaart (German Sand Cake)
description: A cake made with butter or margarine, vanilla or lemon zest, and icing.
steps: Stir the egg yolks completely smooth with the sugar, add the flavoring.
Sift the flour, add the hard butter or margarine in small, equal pieces.
Whip the egg whites as stiffly as possible, stir in the yolks with a few strokes and then, as lightly as possible, the chopped butter or margarine and flour.
Put the batter immediately into a greased tart pan dusted with powdered sugar and flour.

Place the pan in a hot oven, check carefully after 5 minutes to see if the cake is not browning too much, otherwise lay a buttered piece of gray paper on it and bake it light brown and done (25 to 30 minutes).
Test if it is done by inserting a knitting needle, which should come out dry.
Turn the cake out onto a cake rack, let it cool and garnish it if desired with icing and French candied fruits.

title: Eendvogel (Duck)
description: Prepared with duck, butter or margarine, and salt.
steps: Press out the tear glands at the tail until no more fat comes out, or cut them out.
